newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softer in range trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softer in range trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was softer against the dollar in range trading on Monday, with swaps seen on an uptrend on a spillover from Malaysia, dealers said.
They said trading in the spot market was a bit slow, with the tone seen softer although the rupiah was supported on the back of tight money market liquidity.
Spot rupiah was at 2,602/04 at 0245 GMT compared with an opening of 2,590/95. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,601.5/03.5 and 2,601/03, respectively.
The rupiah was in a narrow range between 2,595 and 2,605 and was likely to remain so for the rest of the day, dealers said.
Liquidity remained tight, with overnight money traded at 21.0/22.0 percent in the morning.
Dealers said longer-term swaps were biddish on fears that Bank Indonesia may emulate Bank Negara Malaysia in imposing restrictions on non-trade related swap transactions.

The Malaysian authority has imposed the restrictions starting Monday. It has said banks were required to observe a limit of $2.0 million on outstanding non-commercial related ringgit offer side swap transactions with each foreign customer on a group basis.
"The market is not really active. But we feel the spillover from Malaysia. Overall trading is a bit slow as people are waiting for the Thai package on Tuesday," one said.
Thailand was holding a meeting with IMF to work out a package to revive its ailing aconomy. A final agreement is expected to be submitted for cabinet approval on Tuesday.
One analyst said Thailand remained the region's pressure point and things could settle down only once Thailand showed sign of stability.
However, dealers said the overnight dollar market seemed to be stabilising, with overnight rates traded at 7.5 percent.
Short-dated swaps were slightly up due to tight money market liquidity. Overnight swap was at 0.7/1.0 and tom/next at 0.5/0.6 points.
One-month swap rose to 23.0/26.0 from 18.0/18.5 on Friday, two to 45.0/50.0 from 35.0/40.0, three to 58.0/65.0 from 55.0/59.0 and six to 120.0/128.0 from 114.0/119.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but raised the conversion band to 2,585/2,633 on Friday from 2,575/2,623 on Thursday.
